claim: The one-click demo loads five sample worktrees.
sandbox: fresh browser context; click the primary action; assert five sample rows

claim: Worktrees with blocked agents, remote changes to pull, or local file changes appear before routine worktrees.
sandbox: fresh browser context and bundled sample data; assert the complete deterministic attention order

claim: The sample action and its explanation are visible in the initial desktop and 390px mobile viewport.
sandbox: fresh browser context at 1440x900, 1280x800, and 390x844; measure the full action and explanation inside each viewport

claim: Demo repository data is not sent off the device or saved as real data.
sandbox: fresh browser context; intercept the full demo flow; assert same-origin requests and demo-only session storage

claim: The sample board works offline after its first visit.
sandbox: fresh browser context; load demo once; wait for service worker; set offline; reload and assert five rows

claim: Pulse scans Git metadata and three opt-in adapter fields; it ignores source, prompt, output, and terminal content without changing Git state.
where: landing facts and privacy section, native first-run screen, privacy page, README
sandbox: temporary real Git repository with source, prompt, output, and terminal canaries; run the native scan, assert no canary enters serialized board data, and compare Git and file state before and after

claim: Five worktrees are free and Pulse Pro costs $19 once.
where: landing facts, paid tier, terms, README
sandbox: fresh browser context; assert the free limit and one-time price are shown

claim: The demo works without an account.
sandbox: fresh browser context with no cookies or storage; open the one-click demo and assert the board loads

claim: Pulse Pro shows every worktree and refreshes every 10 seconds.
where: landing paid tier, native limit notice, terms, README
sandbox: eight-worktree fixture; assert free mode returns five, Pro returns all eight, and the production scheduler requests exactly 10000 milliseconds

claim: The public site contacts GitHub only after the visitor requests a release download.
sandbox: fresh browser context with request interception; assert no cross-origin landing requests, click download check, and assert only the GitHub Releases API request

claim: A returned license token stays in local storage and verification sends it only to the Sociobot billing API.
sandbox: fresh browser context with a returned fixture license and mocked Sociobot response; assert URL stripping, namespaced local storage, and the single allowed verification request

claim: License verification runs at most once every 24 hours.
sandbox: fake clock and mocked Sociobot response; assert one request initially, none before 24 hours, and one at 24 hours

claim: An unverified license stays locked if billing verification cannot reach Sociobot.
sandbox: fresh browser context with an uncached fake return token; abort verification, reload offline, and assert the Buy action remains visible with no verdict

claim: An unverified license stays locked when billing rate-limits verification.
sandbox: fresh browser context with an uncached fake return token; return HTTP 429 and assert the Buy action remains visible with no verdict

claim: The download button selects the matching Intel or Apple silicon macOS build.
sandbox: mock GitHub release with both DMGs; use Intel and Apple silicon browser fixtures; assert each direct download URL

claim: The current GitHub release includes a checksum file.
sandbox: fresh checkout; request the public GitHub Releases API and assert the current release and SHA256SUMS are available

claim: The current GitHub release offers macOS, Windows, AppImage, and Debian downloads with checksums.
sandbox: fresh checkout; inspect current public release assets and SHA256SUMS for both macOS builds, Windows, AppImage, and Debian

claim: Every advertised desktop download is checksummed and built from the published release source commit.
where: desktop download section and release metadata
sandbox: public GitHub release API; assert the release target and latest.json source_commit match, then download and hash both macOS DMGs, Windows installer, AppImage, and Debian package

claim: Selecting a real worktree opens a terminal in that exact worktree folder.
where: landing How it works section and README
sandbox: temporary worktree and configured terminal probe; assert the probe receives the selected folder as its working directory

claim: The one-line installers verify SHA-256 before opening or installing a release file.
sandbox: read both shipped installer scripts; assert their checksum rejection check precedes every open, copy, or process-start operation

claim: The desktop app includes no analytics or crash tracking.
sandbox: inspect native and WebView source for network clients and known analytics or crash-tracking endpoints

claim: Remove repository forgets a saved path without changing repository files.
sandbox: temporary Git repository with tracked and untracked canaries; remove its saved path; compare file bytes and Git status before and after

claim: The $19 Pulse Pro purchase link opens a live Dodo checkout.
sandbox: make one live request to the advertised Sociobot checkout URL; require HTTP 303 to an HTTPS checkout.dodopayments.com session

claim: Refund requests use the published Pulse support email.
where: terms page and README privacy and billing section
sandbox: fresh browser context; assert the Terms page exposes the exact mailto refund contact

claim: Repository paths and the license token persist locally; Git and status-file scan results stay in memory.
sandbox: inspect production storage, scan state, and native dependencies; assert paths use the local namespace, board results are not persisted, and the native scanner has no network client

claim: Status files accept working, blocked, and idle; missing or unsupported states are not presented as agent state.
sandbox: temporary status files for every valid value plus invalid and missing states; invoke the native parser and compare serialized state

claim: Development and release builds require Node.js 22 or newer.
where: README setup instructions and package metadata
sandbox: fresh checkout; assert package engine, current runtime, and release workflow all use Node.js 22 or newer

claim: The site build writes a deployable site to dist/site within the JavaScript size budget.
sandbox: fresh checkout; run the production site build; assert dist/site HTML, JavaScript, and CSS exist and JavaScript is at most 200 KB

claim: Version tags build macOS, Windows, AppImage, and Debian desktop bundles in GitHub Actions.
sandbox: inspect the release workflow trigger and OS/architecture bundle matrix

claim: Current macOS and Windows builds are unsigned.
where: landing download section and README install instructions
sandbox: current public release; require unsigned disclosure and runner-generated macOS/Windows signing evidence, with direct PE certificate inspection for older releases

claim: Optional local alerts report a worktree only when its agent changes into blocked state.
sandbox: blocked-state transition fixture; assert one new transition, deduplication of existing blocked state, and opt-in default
